q: What is the CBAM default value for hot-rolled and flat steel from India?
title: CBAM default value: Indian flat steel
short: 4.280 t CO2e per tonne for Indian flat-rolled iron and non-alloy steel under CN 7208 to 7212, direct emissions only. With the 10% mark-up for 2026 that is about 4.708 t. The benchmark route for India is blast furnace and basic oxygen furnace.
audience: Indian HR coil, CR coil, galvanised and plate exporters and their EU importers

sections.h: India default values, t CO2e per tonne
ul: CN 7208 hot-rolled flat, 600 mm and wider: 4.280
CN 7210 coated or plated flat, including galvanised: 4.280
Indirect emissions: not counted for iron and steel

p: The listed values are increased by a mark-up: 10% for 2026, 20% for 2027 and 30% from 2028. Goods imported in 2026 always take the 2026 mark-up.

Defaults are set so they do not understate emissions, and the mark-up adds more. A plant with good fuel and production records will usually come in lower, and only a verified actual figure lets the importer use it.

example.title: 1,000 t of HR coil imported in 2026 on the default

senseible: Senseible reads coal, coke, gas, electricity and freight invoices into a dated, fingerprinted record per site, so an actual figure you send an EU buyer can be traced back to the documents behind it. It does not file CBAM declarations.

sources.label: European Commission, Default values definitive period (Excel, version 2 of 6 August 2026), India sheet; legally binding values in Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1740 correcting (EU) 2025/2621
